## Round g1r1 (2026-11-23)
- Workload: q16 only (count DISTINCT ps_suppkey GROUP BY p_brand,p_type,p_size; partsupp JOIN part, NOT IN supplier MARK join). Baseline 179ms.
- E0001 ACCEPTED: distinct radix HT partitioned on hash(G): -13.4%. Current best 1.155x, q16 ~115-170ms (noisy).
- Facts from earlier db_evolve runs (global auto-memory, same engine):
  - Skip unpartitioned staging for heap (VARCHAR) layouts: ~-5% median, noisy (-15.8, -8.1, +1.6, -5.9).
  - Early HT grow (-3%) and early SkipLookups (<=3%) are noise. Don't repeat.
  - Join output reaches the agg as ~300-row chunks. Main-HT re-sink costs ~150ns/row.
  - Gotcha: wrapping q16 in count(*) lets the optimizer drop DISTINCT. Use max(cnt) instead.
- Code locations: RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:548; AddChunk aggregate_hashtable.cpp:564; FindOrCreateGroupsInternal :641; staging decision :755-761 (radix_bits >= UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD && new/partitions <= 4); Abandon/AcquirePartitionedData Repartition at :108-136.

## Round g1r2 (2026-11-24): profile after E0001 (operator CPU)
- HASH_GROUP_BY 0.31-0.57s (distinct HT only: CanSkipRegularSink skips the main sink when all aggs are DISTINCT).
- Distinct HT key: p_brand compressed to uhugeint, p_type raw VARCHAR (heap layout), p_size utinyint, plus suppkey.
- partsupp scan 0.12-0.28s (8M rows, min/max + hashed BF, emits 1.236M; the join keeps 1.185M).
- E0002 RETIRED: IN list as a scan ExpressionFilter. Correct, but the MARK join is only ~0.01s. Bad target.

## Round g1r3
- E0003 RETIRED: sparse perfect HJ + BF +39..56%. Serial 66MB dictionary build. Bad idea for wide payloads.
- RULE: divide EXPLAIN ANALYZE operator CPU by 8 for a wall-time estimate before predicting gains.
- Perfect HJ facts: range cap 1M (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:108); the duplicate check is off by one; a perfect HJ disables the BF.

## Round g1r4
- E0004 RETIRED (not implemented): measured per-phase CPU in distinct finalize (AggregateDistinctGrouping, physical_hash_aggregate.cpp ~665): distinct GetData 150-168ms, main-HT sink 104ms (88ns/row), Combine 1.5ms. Group-aligned main sink would give <=3.5%. Bad target.
- Combine resets the local HT; the next Sink re-allocates a full sink_capacity pointer table, so per-partition combine is costly.
- Debug tip: Printer::Print output shows up as "ERROR:" on stderr from dbe-tool sql.

## Round g1r5
- Dispatched: staging gate for heap layouts (AllConstant() check at aggregate_hashtable.cpp:755). Low risk, expected -4..-7%.
- Filed in the backlog: count DISTINCT directly from group-aligned distinct partitions (replaces the 104ms main sink). Medium-high risk.
- If the staging gate comes in at noise level, the remaining levers are the distinct-partition count shortcut, the exact bitmap BF (partsupp scan ~20ms wall, <=5%), and p_type dictionary-ID keys.

## Backlog / next ideas
- Exact bitmap BF for dense-int keys (likely <=5% on q16). Earlier runs: q09/q21 -9..-15%; a 128 bits/key cap was needed.
- Distinct-partition count shortcut (see above).
- p_type VARCHAR in the distinct HT key: dictionary-ID group keys or longer-string CM compression.
- Compact ~300-row join output chunks before the agg sink (idea).

issues.title: Skip unpartitioned staging for heap-layout agg HTs
issues.hypothesis: q16's whole runtime is the distinct radix HT, whose key includes the VARCHAR p_type (a heap layout). The join feeds it chunks of about 300 rows. When radix_bits >= UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD and new_entry_count/partitions <= 4, FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:755-761) appends new groups to unpartitioned_data. Abandon/AcquirePartitionedData (lines 108-136) later call Repartition, which copies the rows and the VARCHAR heap again and recomputes pointers. Nearly all (G,x) groups are unique, so every row pays for this. An earlier measurement on this engine (before E0001) gave Abandon 37->2ms and MaybeRepartition 97->56ms CPU, with wall time about -5% median.
issues.plan: In GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp ~line 755), add `layout_ptr->AllConstant()` to the condition that picks unpartitioned_data. Heap layouts then always append straight to partitioned_data. Nothing else changes: when unpartitioned_data stays empty, its Repartition is cheap. Add timers temporarily to check that Abandon/Repartition CPU drops, then run bench 3 times.
issues.expected_gain: q16 -4..-7% (the distinct HT sink plus the main HT sink during distinct finalize both have heap layouts)
issues.generality: Hash aggregates and DISTINCT aggregates with VARCHAR or nested group keys that see many groups or small input chunks. Fixed-width layouts are unchanged. Workloads with few groups per chunk may lose a little append batching on heap layouts.
issues.risk: Low. A one-condition gate. Run the spill and long-string tests: test/sql/aggregate and test/sql/storage spilling.

issues.title: Count DISTINCT directly from group-aligned distinct partitions
issues.hypothesis: E0004's timers: the main-HT sink fed from the distinct scan costs about 104ms CPU, and distinct GetData about 160ms. After E0001, every (G,x) of a given G lands in a single distinct partition, and the finalized partition holds unique (G,x). When every aggregate is a plain count(DISTINCT x) over one shared column, count = the number of non-NULL x per G in that partition, so a cache-resident per-partition counter would replace the 88ns/row main sink.
issues.plan: In HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask::AggregateDistinctGrouping (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp ~665), detect this shape. Then for each scanned distinct partition, group by G with a small per-task HT sized to the partition, and sink only (G,count) into the main HT using a sum-like combine. That needs care, so it may be better to sink pre-aggregated counts as partial states through the count aggregate's combine.
issues.expected_gain: q16 -5..-8% if the 104ms of main-sink CPU mostly disappears
issues.generality: GROUP BY plus count(DISTINCT x) queries with many distinct (G,x) pairs.
issues.risk: Medium to high: it intrudes on the distinct finalize protocol and has to keep NULL handling and the partition alignment exact.
